les: Wat alles in ons water beland
kaps_punt: Waterbesoedeling: in die omgewing, kan baie dinge meng of oplos in water; water kan besoedel word deur: onoplosbare stowwe, soos olie, plastiek, bande, blikkies, glas, toiletafval; oplosbare stowwe soos seep, kunsmis, insekdoders, sure en ander gifstowwe; lewende kieme van toiletafval veroorsaak wateroordraagbare siektes soos diarree

items.bewering: Iemand het dit weggegooi, en die wind of die reën het dit tot by die water gebring. Reënwater loop oor landerye, strate en vullishope voordat dit in 'n rivier of 'n dam beland. Op pad tel dit grond, afval en ander stowwe op en dra dit saam.
items.blok: Hoe dinge in ons water beland
items.bron: UCT Future Water, Cape Town stormwater quality (ICUD 2021): the drainage system carries poor-quality stormwater to rivers; Sowetan/TimesLive 31 Oct 2022: litter washed from Johannesburg's stormwater network into dams in seasonal rain; RePEc 2010 Pretoria runoff study: metals tied to suspended soil solids in runoff; SANBI: dirty urban stormwater among SA's aquatic pollutants.

items.bewering: Afval word soms ook reguit in 'n rivier gegooi.
items.blok: Hoe dinge in ons water beland
items.bron: SANBI, 'Pollution impacts aquatic ecosystems, species and economic activity' (plastics and solid waste in SA's aquatic systems); local reports of litter in the Umgeni River (Daily News).

items.bewering: Toiletafval loop in die water in waar 'n rioolpyp lek of oorloop.
items.blok: Hoe dinge in ons water beland
items.bron: Carroll & Curtis mass-balance study cited for Hartbeespoort Dam (Water SA): recommends refurbishing 'leaking and overflowing sewers'; SANBI lists untreated or poorly treated sewage. The sentence names one route and does not say it is the only one (poorly run treatment works are another), so it is not a false limit.

items.bewering: Ons noem dit besoedeling wanneer stowwe of kieme so in water beland en skade doen.
items.blok: Hoe dinge in ons water beland
items.bron: Dictionary.com/Collins: pollution is the introduction of harmful substances into the environment, contamination of air, water or soil by substances harmful to living organisms; Britannica Dictionary, sense 1 (making water or air dirty and unsafe).

items.bewering: Die eerste soort is onoplosbare stowwe. ... Die tweede soort is oplosbare stowwe ... Die derde soort is kieme.
items.blok: Stukke en lae wat jy kan sien
items.bron: This is the only 'eerste' in the lesson, and it is an ordinal counting the lesson's own three groups, not a claim about rank or history. The three-way split (insoluble substances, soluble substances, living germs from toilet waste) is the one given in the CAPS bullet the lesson copies in kaps_punt. There are no other superlatives in the lesson.

items.bewering: Hulle los nie in water op nie. Hulle bly as stukke of as 'n laag in die water, en jy kan hulle gewoonlik sien.
items.blok: Stukke en lae wat jy kan sien
items.bron: RSC Education / TutorChase on filtration: insoluble matter stays as particles larger than filter pores, while dissolved solute is spread as single ions or molecules. 'gewoonlik' properly covers microplastics and fine suspended matter, which cannot be seen.

items.bewering: Olie meng nie met water nie en vorm 'n laag wat gewoonlik bo-op die water lê.
items.blok: Stukke en lae wat jy kan sien
items.bron: NOAA Office of Response and Restoration, river spill guidance: oil usually floats because it is less dense than water (most oils 0.90-0.98 g/cc), but very heavy oils can sink in a river; IPIECA non-floating oils fact sheet. 'gewoonlik' is exactly the right hedge.

items.bewering: Plastiek breek mettertyd in al kleiner stukkies op, maar dit verdwyn nie.
items.blok: Stukke en lae wat jy kan sien
items.bron: NOAA Marine Debris Program (as reported by Dive Training Magazine): plastics never completely degrade but divide into microplastics; Congressional Research Service IF10967 (citing NOAA): microplastics are particles under 5 mm, including nanoplastics.

items.bewering: Visse, voëls en skilpaaie kan plastiek insluk of daarin vasraak.
items.blok: Stukke en lae wat jy kan sien
items.bron: Congressional Research Service IF10967: wildlife ingest debris (starvation, internal injury, blockage) and become entangled in it; NOAA/Alaska DEC 2011 plastic marine debris fact sheet (seabirds ingesting plastic, fish keeping plastic in their guts); Oceana 2020 analysis of NOAA data (sea turtles).

items.bewering: Ou bande, blikkies en stukkende glas bly as harde stukke in die water.
items.blok: Stukke en lae wat jy kan sien
items.bron: South Carolina DNR 'How long does it take' litter guidance and Clackamas County WES ('If it's on the ground, it's in our water'): tyres, aluminium cans and glass last for decades to centuries and glass breaks into pieces rather than decomposing. Rubber is firm rather than strictly hard, but the point that these stay as solid pieces and do not dissolve holds.

items.bewering: By toiletafval is dit die vaste afval self wat nie oplos nie en in die water bly.
items.blok: Stukke en lae wat jy kan sien
items.bron: Sewage-treatment references (e.g. Northumbrian Water sewage treatment fact sheet; FSM Toolbox sewage treatment design chapter): faecal solids are particulate and settle out as sludge, with only a small fraction in solution. Note: in a river these solids also break down over time, but the claim is about not dissolving, and that is right.

items.bewering: Die tweede soort is oplosbare stowwe soos seep en kunsmis.
items.blok: Gif wat jy nie kan sien nie
items.bron: Soap: Britannica summary 'soap' and LibreTexts soap exemplar (sodium and potassium fatty-acid salts are water-soluble; only heavier-metal soaps, such as hard-water scum, are poorly soluble). Fertiliser: WA Department of Primary Industries, 'Environmental impact of nitrogen and phosphorus fertilisers': most commonly used N and P fertilisers are very soluble.

items.bewering: Sure, party insekdoders en ander gifstowwe is ook oplosbaar.
items.blok: Gif wat jy nie kan sien nie
items.bron: Acid mine drainage (Daily Maverick 17 Mar 2022; Mail & Guardian 23 May 2022) is acidic water carrying dissolved metals and sulphate, i.e. a solution. 'party insekdoders' is correctly hedged, because some insecticides, such as DDT, dissolve poorly in water.

items.bewering: Al hierdie stowwe los in die water op en versprei deur die water. Jy kan hulle dan gewoonlik nie meer sien nie. Water kan dus helder en skoon lyk en steeds besoedel wees.
items.blok: Gif wat jy nie kan sien nie
items.bron: TutorChase/RSC: a solute is dispersed as single ions or molecules (about 0.1-1 nm), far below what can be seen; Daily News 6 Jul 2008, 'Dirty secret lurks under clear water'. 'gewoonlik' covers visible exceptions such as soap foam or coloured dyes.

items.bewering: Jy het ook al geleer dat 'n sif, filtreerpapier of 'n lap nie 'n opgeloste stof uit water kan haal nie.
items.blok: Gif wat jy nie kan sien nie
items.bron: RSC Education (11-14 resource: why a salt solution cannot be separated by filtration); TutorChase AP Chemistry 3.9.1: dissolved solute passes through filter paper with the solvent. The 'you have already learned' framing is curricular, not a fact claim, and was not checked.

items.bewering: Gifstowwe en sure kan plante en diere in die water skaad of doodmaak. Mense kan siek word as hulle sulke water drink.
items.blok: Gif wat jy nie kan sien nie
items.bron: Mail & Guardian 23 May 2022 (Kromdraai acid-mine-water spill killed nearly all aquatic life over about 95 km, from low pH and metal toxicity); Daily Maverick (fish gills destroyed); University of Pretoria via UMP 2022 (fish decline in the upper Olifants). Human illness: the CDC MMWR 2013-2014 drinking-water outbreak surveillance includes chemical and toxin outbreaks.

items.bewering: Kunsmis gee plante stowwe wat hulle nodig het om goed te groei, en tog besoedel dit water. Reën spoel opgeloste kunsmis van landerye en tuine af na riviere en damme.
items.blok: Kunsmis laat waterplante te vinnig groei
items.bron: WA Department of Primary Industries: soluble N and P fertilisers reach waterways by leaching and overland flow; NWU repository thesis on Hartbeespoort Dam: nutrients from runoff from fertilised irrigated land.

items.bewering: In die water laat dit alge en waterplante veel te vinnig groei. Hulle kan dan 'n dam of 'n stil stuk rivier oorgroei.
items.blok: Kunsmis laat waterplante te vinnig groei
items.bron: NIVA MADMACS Hartbeespoort project update: severe eutrophication from wastewater, sewage spills and fertiliser runoff drives excessive water hyacinth and algae; Rhodes University news on Hartbeespoort's hyacinth invasion; Water SA articles on the dam. Fertiliser is a real contributor, though in Hartbeespoort sewage is the larger one. The lesson claims only that fertiliser does it, which is true.

items.bewering: Kieme is nie 'n stof wat oplos of nie oplos nie, maar baie klein lewende dinge. Toiletafval kan lewende kieme dra. Kieme is te klein om met jou oë te sien.
items.blok: Kieme uit toiletafval
items.bron: Merriam-Webster Medical, 'germ': a microorganism, especially one causing disease (bacterium, virus); WHO diarrhoeal disease fact sheet: water contaminated with human faeces is of particular concern, from bacterial, viral and parasitic organisms. Note: whether viruses are 'living' is debated, but the CAPS bullet itself says 'lewende kieme', and the lesson never claims anything about every germ.

items.bewering: Water kan dus skoon lyk en tog kieme dra. Iemand kan 'n wateroordraagbare siekte soos diarree kry deur sulke water te drink.
items.blok: Kieme uit toiletafval
items.bron: WHO fact sheet 'Diarrhoeal disease': infection is spread through contaminated drinking water, and microorganisms are invisible without magnification (Merriam-Webster; Developing Experts glossary 'germs').

items.bewering: So 'n siekte kry 'n mens deur water te drink of te gebruik waarin iets is wat mense siek maak.
items.blok: Kieme uit toiletafval
items.bron: The sources disagree on what 'waterborne disease' covers. Narrow sense: Wikipedia 'Waterborne diseases' (lead: 'diseases caused by pathogenic micro-organisms'; chemical pollutants are treated separately, and 'water-related disease' is the wider category) and several glossaries limit it to disease caused by pathogens spread by drinking, washing or bathing. Broad sense: the CDC MMWR drinking-water outbreak surveillance (2013-2014) counts chemical and toxin outbreaks as waterborne disease outbreaks, and one legal definition (Law Insider) includes chemical, physical and radiological agents. 'iets wat mense siek maak' takes the broad reading, so it would make acid or poison in water a waterborne disease. Under the narrow, health-science reading that is wrong. The part about drinking OR USING the water is right under both readings.
items.regstelling: A wording that is true under both definitions ties the disease to germs, for example: 'So 'n siekte kry 'n mens deur water te drink of te gebruik waarin kieme is wat mense siek maak.' A person should decide whether to narrow it like this or accept the broad reading.

items.bewering: Nie alle diarree kom van kieme in water nie, maar besoedelde water is een manier waarop mense dit kry.
items.blok: Kieme uit toiletafval
items.bron: WHO fact sheet 'Diarrhoeal disease': spread through contaminated food or drinking water, or person to person through poor hygiene; diarrhoea is 'usually' a symptom of infection, so non-infectious causes also exist.

items.bewering: Onoplosbare stowwe bly as stukke of as 'n laag wat jy gewoonlik kan sien.
items.blok: Drie soorte besoedeling in water
items.bron: Same sources as the 'Stukke en lae wat jy kan sien' items (RSC/TutorChase on particles; NOAA on oil layers).

items.bewering: Oplosbare stowwe los op, en jy kan hulle gewoonlik nie sien nie.
items.blok: Drie soorte besoedeling in water
items.bron: TutorChase / RSC Education: dissolved solute is spread as single ions or molecules.

items.bewering: Kieme is lewende dinge wat te klein is om te sien en mense siek kan maak.
items.blok: Drie soorte besoedeling in water
items.bron: Merriam-Webster Medical 'germ'; Developing Experts glossary 'germs' (tiny living things that can cause disease, invisible to the naked eye).

items.bewering: Iets skadeliks wat in die omgewing beland, soos stowwe of kieme in water, lug of grond.
items.blok: besoedeling
items.bron: Britannica Dictionary 'pollution', sense 2: the substances that make land, water or air dirty and unsafe; Collins (via Dictionary.com): contamination of air, water or soil by harmful substances. Pollution can also be energy (noise, heat, light), but 'soos' introduces examples and does not close the list.

items.bewering: Iets wat in water kan oplos, soos suiker en sout.
items.blok: oplosbaar
items.bron: RSC Education / Oak National Academy Year 5 'separating soluble solids from solutions' (salt dissolves and passes through filter paper). Strictly, solubility is relative to any solvent, but defining it for water is right within this lesson's scope.

items.bewering: Iets wat nie in water oplos nie, soos sand.
items.blok: onoplosbaar
items.bron: RSC Education filtration resources (sand is the standard insoluble solid separated by filtration).

items.bewering: Baie klein lewende dinge wat 'n mens siek kan maak.
items.blok: kieme
items.bron: Merriam-Webster Medical 'germ': a microorganism causing disease; Developing Experts glossary. 'kan' avoids saying every germ makes people sick. Viruses are borderline as 'living', as noted under 'Kieme uit toiletafval'; CAPS uses 'lewende kieme'.

items.bewering: 'n Siekte wat 'n mens kan kry deur water te drink of te gebruik waarin iets is wat mense siek maak, soos kieme.
items.blok: wateroordraagbare siekte
items.bron: Same conflict as the matching sentence in 'Kieme uit toiletafval'. The usual health-science definition (Wikipedia 'Waterborne diseases', most glossaries) means disease caused by pathogens and puts chemical poisoning under the wider 'water-related'. The CDC's drinking-water outbreak surveillance and a legal definition also count chemicals and toxins. In this entry 'soos kieme' makes germs only ONE example of 'iets wat mense siek maak', so it states the broad reading outright. This entry is read on its own, so it is the place where the difference would matter in a test answer.
items.regstelling: A wording true under both definitions: ''n Siekte wat 'n mens kan kry deur water te drink of te gebruik waarin kieme is wat mense siek maak.' A person should decide whether to narrow it or accept the broad reading, and should handle this entry and the study-block sentence the same way.

items.bewering: 'n Stof wat mense by grond voeg sodat plante beter groei.
items.blok: kunsmis
items.bron: WA Department of Primary Industries (fertilisers applied to soils and pastures to supply N and P); Dictionary.com 'fertilizer'. Spraying it on leaves or using it in hydroponics are exceptions not needed at this level.

items.bewering: 'n Middel wat mense gebruik om insekte dood te maak.
items.blok: insekdoder
items.bron: Standard definition of an insecticide (a substance used to kill insects), consistent with Merriam-Webster; nothing in the sources consulted qualifies it.

items.bewering: 'n Stof wat 'n lewende ding siek kan maak of kan doodmaak.
items.blok: gifstof
items.bron: Mail & Guardian / Daily Maverick 2022 on metal toxicity killing aquatic life; matches the sense of poison/toxic substance in Collins and Merriam-Webster. In Afrikaans 'gifstof' means poison generally, not only a toxin of biological origin, so the wide definition is right.

opsomming: Every claim but one checks out: the lesson twice defines a waterborne disease as one you get from water containing 'something that makes people sick, such as germs', and while the usual health-science definition limits it to germs (pathogens), the CDC and a legal definition also count chemicals, so a person must choose between narrowing both places to germs (true under both readings) and accepting the broad reading; there are no analogies in the lesson, and its only 'eerste' is an ordinal counting its three groups.
